newsitem.title: USA: BA says no timetable for pact approval.
newsitem.headline: BA says no timetable for pact approval.

text.p: British Airways Plc Chairman Sir Colin Marshall said the airline had no idea when its proposed alliance with American Airlines may be approved.
"We have no specific timetable that we can work to," Marshall told reporters after a New York press conference to unveil a new corporate logo and aircraft designs.

"I think the process that is taking place now is that our new government in Britain is assimilating the case because until they came in to office, they did not get directly involved in the issues and in the facts," Marshall said.

British Airways and AMR Corp's American Airlines last year announced plans to form a far-reaching marketing alliance, which they originally hoped would begin in April. But the approval process has bogged down amid regulatory scrutiny, and there is no current target date for approval.
The proposed alliance is being studied by British and U.S. regulators as well as the European Commission. In Britain, a new Labour Party government was swept to power on May 1.
Marshall reiterated British Airways' stance that it may forego the proposed alliance if regulators require the airlines to pay a burdensome price.

"We have always said that if the regulatory costs are going to be too great, we're going to have to give serious consideration to walking away. But we certainly hope that this is not going to be the case," Marshall said.
Marshall said other pacts, such as the Star Alliance which includes UAL Corp's United Airlines and Deutsche Lufthansa AG, have faced less scrutiny.
The Star Alliance "has all gone forward and the regulators haven't challenged it, and here we are with American stuck in a rut waiting for the regulators to come to their positions."

Separately, British Airways announced a $10 billion makeover plan to be phased in over the next three years. In addition to buying 43 new Boeing Co aircraft, the carrier unveiled a new corporate logo and a range of international designs for its airplanes.

In a effort to promote British Airways as a more global airline, the company's fleet of about 300 jets now will have a diverse look. The tails of the aircraft will feature more than 50 designs, ranging from a Scottish tartan to Chinese calligraphy, commissioned from artists around the world.
The makeover will be the first facelift since BA swapped the national flag for its staid design of blue, red and gray in 1984, as the airline prepared for privatization.

British Airways said it set aside $3.2 million for the images and the overall design. The actual fleet makeover will cost $98 million over three years, although much of that would have been spent anyway on regular painting, the company said.
British Airways said the new airplane design reflects its increasingly international focus, with about 60 percent of its customers coming from outside Britain.
